concepts.name: Breach notification deadline in force on 15 September 2026
justifications: Section 8.1 of the original DPA sets a 48-hour outer limit, and Amendment No. 1 (which replaces it with 24 hours) only takes effect on 1 October 2026, so the 48-hour limit is still in force on 15 September 2026.

concepts.name: Breach notification deadline in force on 1 November 2026
justifications: Amendment No. 1 replaces Section 8.1 with a 24-hour outer limit, effective 1 October 2026, which is in force on 1 November 2026.

concepts.name: Audit notice period in force on 1 November 2026
justifications: Amendment No. 1 reduces the on-site audit notice period under Section 10.2 from 30 days to 20 days, effective 1 October 2026.

concepts.name: Liability cap in force on 1 November 2026
justifications: Amendment No. 1 replaces Section 13.1 with a Processor aggregate liability cap of EUR 1,000,000, which is in force on 1 November 2026 and does not depend on fees paid.

concepts.name: Liability cap covers confidentiality breaches
justifications: The replacement Section 13.1 expressly excludes breaches of Section 4 (Confidentiality) from the EUR 1,000,000 cap, so the cap does not cover confidentiality breaches.

concepts.name: Meridian Mail approved on 1 November 2026
justifications: Meridian Mail Ltd is listed in Annex 3 as an approved Sub-processor from the Effective Date, and its withdrawal only takes effect on 1 January 2027.

concepts.name: Meridian Mail approved on 1 February 2027
justifications: Amendment No. 1 withdraws approval of Meridian Mail Ltd with effect from 1 January 2027, so it is no longer an approved Sub-processor on 1 February 2027.

concepts.name: Distinct data locations count as of 1 February 2027
justifications: As of 1 February 2027, data is stored in Norway and Estonia, processing occurs in Lithuania, and France and Denmark were added as approved Sub-processor locations effective 1 January 2027, while Ireland's approval was withdrawn.

concepts.name: Deletion deadline for year-end termination
justifications: Under Section 12.1 as amended by A5.1 (effective 1 October 2026), deletion or return is due within 60 days of termination, which counted from 31 December 2026 ends on 1 March 2027.

concepts.name: Breach notification obligation summary
predicted: the processor must notify the controller of a personal data breach affecting data processed under the dpa without undue delay and no later than 24 hours after becoming aware of it.
gold: the processor must notify the controller without undue delay and within 24 hours after becoming aware of a personal data breach affecting data processed under the dpa, describing its nature, affected categories and approximate numbers of data subjects and records, likely consequences, and measures taken or proposed to address the breach and mitigate its effects. it must document all breaches and cooperate with any regulatory notifications or data subject communications the controller determines are required.
values: The Processor must notify the Controller of a personal data breach affecting data processed under the DPA without undue delay and no later than 24 hours after becoming aware of it.
justifications: This summary restates the amended Section 8.1 as in force on 1 November 2026, which sets a 24-hour outer limit for initial notification.

concepts.name: Applicable initial notification regime
justifications: Usable privileged credentials exposure was confirmed, which triggers the expedited 12-hour outer limit for initial notification of this breach. The standard 24-hour limit applies only to breaches without that confirmed exposure.

concepts.name: Initial notice lateness in minutes
justifications: Verified unauthorised access at 17:10 on 9 April 2027 set awareness, so the 12-hour expedited limit expired at 05:10 on 10 April. The first notice was delivered at 06:00 that day, 50 minutes later.

concepts.name: Completed follow-up report deadline
justifications: Awareness on Friday 9 April 2027 makes the follow-up due at the end of the third counted Business Day. Excluding the 12 April closure and the only approved pause day (14 April), the counted days are 13, 15 and 16 April.

concepts.name: Held ORD records deletion deadline
justifications: The held ORD records must be deleted by the later of the ordinary deletion deadline (60 days from the 30 June 2027 termination, i.e. 29 August 2027) and the tenth Business Day after the last hold ends on 25 August 2027, which is 8 September 2027.

concepts.name: BK-0630 deletion deadline
justifications: Backup BK-0630 contains no held records, so it must be deleted by the earlier of its ordinary deletion deadline and 35 calendar days after its creation on 30 June 2027, which is 4 August 2027. Restoration does not extend this period.

concepts.name: Permitted uses of held ORD records on 1 September 2027
justifications: After termination, records retained solely under a legal hold may be used only for legal preservation, and analytics was expressly rejected for the held ORD records. Service delivery is not permitted for these records.

concepts.name: Nordlicht infrastructure approval start
justifications: Approval for the Stockholm service begins no earlier than the latest of the proposed start date, completed security review, and written consent. The security review completed on 22 April, which is the latest of these conditions.

concepts.name: Ordinary customer email providers on 10 May 2027
justifications: Cendrillon Mail SAS was added as an approved Sub-processor for transactional email from 1 January 2027 and continues that service. Meridian Mail Ltd's approval was withdrawn and its emergency permission does not cover ordinary email on 10 May 2027.

concepts.name: Authorised data locations on 15 May 2027
justifications: These countries have actual processing (Norway storage, Estonia and Lithuania facilities, France email, Sweden Stockholm infrastructure) and effective authorisation on 15 May 2027. Denmark's authorisation was withdrawn, Ireland's emergency permission expired, and Finland and Germany have no started processing.

concepts.name: Written consent date for Nordlicht email in Finland
Security cap before earlier payments in EUR
justifications: The security cap is the greater of EUR 2,000,000 and twice the Qualifying Fees, which are EUR 1,200,000 excluding VAT less the EUR 60,000 credit, giving EUR 1,140,000 and a doubled amount of EUR 2,280,000. Training and prepaid April 2027 fees are excluded.

concepts.name: Ordinary cap remaining before new claims in EUR
justifications: The ordinary cap of EUR 1,000,000 per Contract Year is reduced by the EUR 300,000 ordinary payments already made in the current Contract Year beginning 1 March 2027. The February 2027 payment belongs to the preceding year and does not count.

concepts.name: Total payable on new claims in EUR
justifications: Ordinary loss L-1 is limited to the remaining EUR 700,000 ordinary pool. The security loss of EUR 1,750,000 (counted once) fits the remaining EUR 1,780,000 security pool, and the two confidentiality-related losses of EUR 250,000 and EUR 100,000 are uncapped under the confidentiality precedence rule.
